title: Decoupled Rationalization with Asymmetric Learning Rates: A Flexible Lipschitz Restraint

problem.claim: Self-explaining rationalization models use a generator to select text rationales and a predictor to make predictions from them.

gap.claim: The cooperative game can degenerate when the predictor overfits to uninformative pieces from an undertrained generator, causing the generator to converge to a sub-optimal model that selects senseless pieces.

contributions.claim: The paper theoretically connects degeneration with the predictor's Lipschitz continuity.
It proposes DR, a method that restrains the predictor's Lipschitz constant to address degeneration.
DR decouples the generator and predictor by assigning them asymmetric learning rates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two widely used benchmarks reportedly verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rationalization models jointly select human-intelligible text pieces and predict from the selected rationales.
Predictor overfitting to early uninformative selections can cause degeneration and senseless rationales.
Degeneration is theoretically linked to predictor Lipschitz continuity.
DR restrains the predictor's Lipschitz constant by decoupling generator and predictor learning with asymmetric rates.
Experiments on two benchmarks are reported to support the method's effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Jointly trained components can reinforce early errors when one component is not yet well trained.

interpretation.claim: Training dynamics and component coupling can create degeneration beyond the intended modeling objective.

application.claim: Consider controlling component coupling or using asymmetric optimization schedules in jointly trained systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether asymmetric learning rates generalize beyond this rationalization setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the theoretical conditions connecting degeneration and Lipschitz continuity.
The abstract does not provide benchmark names, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details of DR or its learning-rate settings.
